The second: except with justice (al-adl). This is transmitted (ma'thur).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 46, verse 7–9:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: its meaning is, "I am not the first of the messengers."

Al-bidʿ (novelty) means "the first."

Al-badīʿ (the originator) of anything is al-mubtadiʿ (the one who initiates it). Qutrub recited, citing ʿAdiyy ibn Zayd:

"So I am not a novelty among the calamities that befall men, which after my misery have turned them into the most fortunate."

﴿And I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾. Concerning this there are four interpretations:

The first: it means, "I do not know what will be done with me or with you in this world, not in the Hereafter. I do not know whether I will be expelled as the prophets before me were expelled, or killed as the prophets before me were killed; and I do not know what will be done with you, whether you will be believers or deniers, whether you will be punished or deferred." This was said by al-Hasan.

The second: "I do not know what will be done with me or with you in the Hereafter."

This was before the revelation of ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾, the verse.

When that was revealed to him in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, he knew what would be done with him in the Hereafter, and he said to his companions: "There has been revealed to me a verse more beloved to me than all the world," and when he recited it, a man from the people said: "Congratulations, O Messenger of Allah! Allah has explained what He will do with you, so what will He do with us?" Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, the verse.

This was said by Qatadah.

The third: that the Prophet ﷺ said before the Hijrah: "I saw in my dream a land to which I would emigrate from Makkah." When the trial grew severe upon his companions in Makkah, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, how long shall we endure this trial? And when will you go out to the land you saw?" He ﷺ said: "I do not know what will be done with me or with you; will we die in Makkah or will we be driven out from it." This was said by al-Kalbi.

The fourth: its meaning is, "Say: I do not know what I am commanded to do, nor what you are commanded to do." This was said by al-Dahhak.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 46, verse 10–14:

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One: If the Qur'an is from Allah and you disbelieve in it. This was said by Yahya.

The second: If Muhammad ﷺ is a prophet from Allah and you disbelieve in him. This was said by al-Sha'bi.

﴿And a witness from the Children of Israel testified to its like﴾. Regarding this there are five opinions:

The first: he is 'Abdullah ibn Salam, who testified against the Jews that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is mentioned in the Torah. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and Mujahid.

The second: he is Amin ibn Yamin, who said when 'Abdullah ibn Salam embraced Islam: "I am a witness like his testimony and a believer like his belief." This was said by al-Suddi.

The third: Musa, like Muhammad ﷺ, bears witness to his prophethood, and the Torah, like the Qur'an, bears witness to its truthfulness. This was said by Masruq.

The poet said:

Regarding the root of uff and taff, there are three aspects:

The first: uff is the wax of the ear, and taff is the dirt of the nose.

The second: uff is the dirt of the fingernails, and taff is what is found at the roots of the fingernails.

The third: uff is one whose nose is sick, and taff is distancing.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 46, verses 33–35:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So be patient, as the resolute among the messengers were patient﴾. Regarding it there are six opinions:

The first: that the resolute (ulu al-'azm) among the messengers are the prophets who were commanded to fight, as said by al-Suddi and al-Kalbi.

The second: that they are the Arab prophets, as said by Mujahid and al-Sha'bi.

The third: those among the prophets whom no trial afflicted, as said by al-Hasan.

The fourth: those among them who were struck by affliction without sin, as said by Ibn Jurayj.

The fifth: that they are the resolute (ulu al-'azm), related by Yahya.

The sixth: that they are the people of patience (ulu al-sabr) who endured the harm of their people and did not lament.

'A'isha related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, was not pleased with the resolute among the messengers except through patience in what they disliked and patience in what was hidden from them." Regarding who the resolute among them are, there are six sayings:

The first: that all the prophets were resolute, and God did not send a messenger except that he was among the resolute.

So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to be patient as they were patient, as said by Ibn Zayd.

The second: that the resolute among them are Noah, Hud and Abraham, so God commanded His Messenger to be the fourth of them, as said by Abu al-'Aliya.

The third: that they are Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The fourth: that they are Noah, Hud, Abraham, Shu'ayb and Moses, as said by 'Abd al-'Aziz.

The fifth: that they are Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, Jesus and Muhammad, may the prayers of God be upon them, as said by al-Suddi.

(p-289) The sixth: that among them are Ishmael, Jacob and Job, and that Jonah, Solomon and Adam are not among them, as said by Ibn Jurayj.

﴿And do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them﴾. Regarding it there are two aspects:

The first: by invoking [God's curse] upon them, as said by Muqatil.

The second: by [seeking] the punishment, and this is a threat.

﴿As if, on the day they see what they are promised﴾. Regarding it there are two aspects:

The first: [what they are promised] is the punishment, as said by Yahya.

The second: [what they are promised] is the Hereafter, as said by al-Naqqash.

﴿They will not have remained but an hour of a day﴾. Regarding it there are two aspects:

The first: [they will not have remained] in the world until the punishment came upon them, which is the implication of Yahya's saying.

The second: [they will not have remained] in their graves until they are raised for the reckoning, which is the implication of al-Naqqash's saying.

﴿A proclamation﴾. Regarding it there are three aspects:

The first: that this remaining is a proclamation, as said by Ibn 'Isa.

The second: that this Qur'an is a proclamation, as said by al-Hasan.

The third: that this which God has described is a proclamation, and it is the arrival of what He promised, either of destruction in the world or of punishment in the Hereafter, according to the two aspects mentioned earlier. ﴿Will any be destroyed﴾, meaning after this proclamation?

﴿Except the defiantly disobedient people﴾. Yahya said: the polytheists.

Muqatil mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, and God commanded him to be patient over what had afflicted him, as the resolute among the messengers were patient, as an ease for him and a strengthening of him. And God knows best.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So be patient, as the resolute among the messengers were patient﴾. Regarding it there are six opinions:

The first: that the resolute (ulu al-'azm) among the messengers are the prophets who were commanded to fight, as said by al-Suddi and al-Kalbi.

The second: that they are the Arab prophets, as said by Mujahid and al-Sha'bi.

The third: those among the prophets whom no trial afflicted, as said by al-Hasan.

The fourth: those among them who were struck by affliction without sin, as said by Ibn Jurayj.

The fifth: that they are the resolute (ulu al-'azm), related by Yahya.

The sixth: that they are the people of patience (ulu al-sabr) who endured the harm of their people and did not lament.

'A'isha related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, was not pleased with the resolute among the messengers except through patience in what they disliked and patience in what was hidden from them." Regarding who the resolute among them are, there are six sayings:

The first: that all the prophets were resolute, and God did not send a messenger except that he was among the resolute.

So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to be patient as they were patient, as said by Ibn Zayd.

The second: that the resolute among them are Noah, Hud and Abraham, so God commanded His Messenger to be the fourth of them, as said by Abu al-'Aliya.

The third: that they are Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The fourth: that they are Noah, Hud, Abraham, Shu'ayb and Moses, as said by 'Abd al-'Aziz.

The fifth: that they are Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, Jesus and Muhammad, may the prayers of God be upon them, as said by al-Suddi.

(p-289) The sixth: that among them are Ishmael, Jacob and Job, and that Jonah, Solomon and Adam are not among them, as said by Ibn Jurayj.

﴿And do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them﴾. Regarding it there are two aspects:

The first: by invoking [God's curse] upon them, as said by Muqatil.

The second: by [seeking] the punishment, and this is a threat.

﴿As if, on the day they see what they are promised﴾. Regarding it there are two aspects:

The first: [what they are promised] is the punishment, as said by Yahya.

The second: [what they are promised] is the Hereafter, as said by al-Naqqash.

﴿They will not have remained but an hour of a day﴾. Regarding it there are two aspects:

The first: [they will not have remained] in the world until the punishment came upon them, which is the implication of Yahya's saying.

The second: [they will not have remained] in their graves until they are raised for the reckoning, which is the implication of al-Naqqash's saying.

﴿A proclamation﴾. Regarding it there are three aspects:

The first: that this remaining is a proclamation, as said by Ibn 'Isa.

The second: that this Qur'an is a proclamation, as said by al-Hasan.

The third: that this which God has described is a proclamation, and it is the arrival of what He promised, either of destruction in the world or of punishment in the Hereafter, according to the two aspects mentioned earlier. ﴿Will any be destroyed﴾, meaning after this proclamation?

﴿Except the defiantly disobedient people﴾. Yahya said: the polytheists.
